title: ArcadiaCloud reseller routing & compatibility discovery
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and ArcadiaCloud to understand reseller integration requirements, routing/policy preferences, and compatibility constraints for a channel partnership. Covered dedicated vs hosted routing, VPC peering, billing/usage attribution, and enterprise security needs (SSO, KMS, audit logs). Agreed to run a compatibility checklist and a small validation POC for routing behavior and billing attribution.
topics: routing policies: latency vs cost vs region
VPC/on-prem connection options and network peering
compatibility matrix for Arcadia offerings and Redwood Dedicated/Private
next steps: compatibility checklist + POC scope
next_steps: Redwood to send partner compatibility checklist and mapping template (Maya) — due 2027-01-14
ArcadiaCloud to provide sample billing/usage CSV and account structure (Tom) — due 2027-01-17
Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with Arcadia infra team and Redwood SEs (Ravi/Lena) — target week of 2027-01-24
Agree on POC success criteria for routing and attribution (joint) — bring to deep-dive
action_items: Maya Chen - share partner checklist + Redwood Dedicated vs Private one-pager - 2027-01-14
Ravi Patel - prep high-level network diagram options (VPC peering, private link, on-prem tunnel) - 2027-01-20
Tom Hsu - export example billing structure and reseller account nesting - 2027-01-17
Priya Iyer - list compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO, KMS preferences) for Arcadia enterprise customers - 2027-01-18
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Tom Hsu (Arcadia), Jenna Morales (Arcadia), Lucas Nguyen (Arcadia), Priya Iyer (Arcadia)

Summary (auto): Intro, clarify reseller integration models, routing, security.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. i'm Maya from Redwood, account lead on partners. quick round of intros?
[00:10] Tom: yeah tom here, head of partnerships at ArcadiaCloud, we run a reseller channel for managed cloud and want to understand how Redwood could slot into our product stack and also what the operational bits look like.
[00:22] Jenna: jenna, product lead, i'll be driving the technical requirements from our end and coordinating the POC.
[00:28] Lucas: lucas, infra, i'll focus on networking and deployment compatibility.
[00:33] Priya: priya from security, i'll look for the compliance checklist, sso, kms, audit logs.
[00:38] Maya: great, and r7... r- ravi and lena are here on the engineering side to do the deep parts. r- ravi, quick hello?
[00:46] Ravi: hey all, ravi - i'll be your main SE on networking, routing policy, and perf stuff.
[00:50] Lena: lena, observability and billing attribution questions are my wheelhouse.

[01:05] Maya: Agenda — understand Arcadia's reseller model (how accounts are nested), expected routing rules (do you route by latency or by cost?), security & compliance, and what a small validation POC would look like.

[01:20] Tom: high level, Arcadia sells managed cloud regions to mid-market and enterprises. we sometimes resell partner inference as an add-on; important is that customers see Arcadia as the bill owner, even if compute runs in partner infra. so billing attribution and tagging is critical.
[01:40] Jenna: we also have some customers with strict data residency, so we'd need the option to pin inference traffic to specific regions or our on-prem options.
[01:50] Maya: got it. Redwood has three deployment modes — hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). for reseller workflows you can map to either Dedicated or Private depending on isolation. the hosted path could work for self-serve SMB but not for white-labeled billing typically.
[02:10] Lucas: can you expand on the private deployment? the term private sometimes means many things. is that a customer-managed control plane?
[02:18] Ravi: yeah, so Redwood Private can be deployed into a customer VPC or on-prem via our private control plane, we support VPC peering and privatelink style connections. we also have an optional on-prem bundle for fully air-gapped setups. note: some customers call it "red wood private" in notes, so apologies if i say it weird.
[02:38] Priya: how about keys and encryption — do you integrate with external KMS? audit logs retention?
[02:44] Lena: we do KMS integration, support customer-managed keys (we've done kms/hsm integrations). audit logs are available via the console and can stream to your SIEM; retention tiers are configurable as an add-on.

[03:05] Jenna: one pain we have: reseller billing attribution. if Arcadia is the bill owner but the workload runs on Redwood Dedicated capacity, can you surface per-customer usage in a way we can ingest?
[03:18] Lena: yes — we can emit per-token usage by token-level tagging and produce usage exports (CSV/JSON). small caveat is that to keep latency and batching optimal we use prefix KV caching and batching heuristics; tagging needs to be part of the request metadata so it survives batching. sometimes the transcription reads KV cache as K V cake in our notes, haha.
[03:38] Tom: ok so we need mapping from Arcadia account ids to Redwood customer ids, and ideally a sample csv to see fields.
[03:45] Maya: we'll share a partner mapping template after the call.

[04:10] Lucas: networking — if we set up VPC peering, what's the routing behavior? do you support routing rules where low-latency customers get pinned to the nearest Dedicated pool while cost-sensitive ones route to a cheaper region?
[04:25] Ravi: yep. Redwood supports policy-based routing. policies can be based on customer tier, latency SLO, or cost budget. we support automatic fallback to regional variants if capacity is constrained. important to understand is that routing decisions are made at the gateway level; for pinned workloads we can ensure sticky routing to the dedicated pool.
[04:48] Jenna: if routing shifts mid-request (like fallback), how do you preserve session state / KV cache?
[04:55] Ravi: good q — we keep KV cache affinity by session token and we do continuous batching and kv cache replication across compatible backends. there are edge cases if you switch to a different model family where kv cache isn't compatible; in that case we stream the last token and rewarm the cache, but we'd rather avoid for a given session.

[05:20] Tom: any gotchas around model variants? e.g. we may want to fallback from a quantized variant to a full fp16 model for quality reasons.
[05:26] Ravi: yes, model-variant fallbacks are supported but require compatibility mapping. we'll want to document preferred fallbacks in the config so you don't get surprising quality shifts.

[05:40] Priya: security checklist — SSO / SAML support, RBAC (we need reseller-level role separation), SOC2 evidence, certs, and access logs. can we get an SOC2 report in early NDA?
[05:55] Maya: for enterprise partners we typically share SOC2 under an NDA; we can kick off that request. SAML/SSO is supported, RBAC is configurable by role for the Console.
[06:06] Priya: and are audit logs tamper-evident?
[06:09] Lena: logs are append-only in our system and can be forwarded to your logging endpoint. we also support signed log exports if your compliance team needs them.

[06:30] Jenna: operations — what does a pilot look like? we want to run a 30-day validation hitting routing rules and billing attribution with 2-3 customers.
[06:41] Maya: common pilot is: one test Arcadia account + two customer accounts. validate network connectivity, confirm routing policies (latency vs cost), verify usage exports and billing. Redwood provides a test harness and can run a small load gen to simulate traffic.
[06:55] Tom: timeline — we are aiming to have a partner pilot ready in feb if the legal path is straightforward.
[07:02] Maya: that works. we'll put dates in the checklist.

[07:20] Ravi: quick technical nit — if you plan to use VPC peering to Dedicated pools in a different cloud region, watch out for egress charges and a potential latency hit. sometimes our partners choose to deploy Dedicated pools in multiple regions to avoid that.
[07:35] Lucas: understood, we'll map out expected traffic patterns.

[07:50] Lena: on billing attribution, we'll need to know if Arcadia wants to rebrand invoices or have a nested reseller model where Arcadia gets a consolidated bill and customers get zero-charge invoices from Redwood — we support both but it's a config conversation.
[08:05] Tom: we want consolidated billing to Arcadia, yes. customers should see Arcadia as the vendor.
[08:11] Maya: fine, we'll include our billing mapping template.

[08:25] Jenna: do you have a short doc on how Redwood's Optimize recommends batching/quantization per workload?
[08:33] Ravi: yes, Redwood Optimize is our toolkit that looks at token distributions and recommends batching and quantization. we'll send a one-pager; note sometimes internal notes call it "redwood optimise" spelled differently.

[08:50] Priya: legal concerns — processor/sub-processor list? any downstream cloud partners you rely on?
[08:59] Maya: we'll provide the processor list and a standard DPA. we also publish a list of cloud infra partners, and can show network diagrams.

[09:20] Tom: great. last quick Q — is there a resell margin or partner pricing program?
[09:28] Maya: we have partner pricing for committed Dedicated capacity and a reseller pricing program for private deployments. i'll surface the commercial motion in follow-up (sales/partnerships doc).

[09:40] Jenna: good. sounds like enough to move to the technical deep-dive.
[09:45] Maya: recap of next steps: we'll send the partner compatibility checklist, Redwood team will prepare network options and a POC plan, Arcadia sends billing samples and compliance list. set up deep-dive for week of jan 24.
[09:58] Tom: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:02] Maya: thanks all, closing.

Notes: occasional transcription errors observed (product names, acronyms). references shared: partner checklist draft (link: https://redwood.example.com/partner-checklist), billing mapping template (link: https://redwood.example.com/billing-template).
